title: Partner quickstatus — recovery choices and verification (draft)
body:
Audience: external partners + customer engineering contacts (concise, actionable).

One-line summary:
We experienced a transient inference-consistency regression affecting multipart responses for ~70 minutes in eu-west-1 on 2029-05-12. The service is currently restored to primary behavior; this doc outlines verified recovery actions, verification steps you can run, and opt-in replay/rollback choices for customers who want historical request re-processing.

Impact (what customers saw):
- Sporadic truncated or duplicated tokens in streaming responses for some multi-chunk requests (chat & structured streaming).
- ~0.5% of requests in the affected time window returned inconsistent structured outputs (field order or missing optional fields).
- No data loss; request payloads and logs retained for auditing.

Current status (as of last_modified):
- Primary mitigation applied at 2029-05-12T11:07:00Z (kernel routing rule corrected).
- Monitoring indicates error rates back to baseline in eu-west-1; short-lived residual retries observed but within SLA.
- Post-incident automated validation runs are green (schema checks and token-consistency tests).

What happened (high level timeline):
1) 2029-05-12T09:54Z — First anomalous alerts: elevated streaming truncation errors.
2) 2029-05-12T10:02Z — Ops triage: confirmed candidate regression after a kernel selection change in release INF-KERNEL-2029-05-12-A.
3) 2029-05-12T10:45Z — Rollback of kernel routing change to previous stable profile.
4) 2029-05-12T11:07Z — Additional guard added to routing logic; monitoring shows recovery.
5) 2029-05-12T13:00Z — Longer tail validation completed; decision to offer targeted replay for affected tenants.

Why this matters for you (partner view):
- If your integration uses structured streaming or relies on deterministic field ordering, you may see a small number of user-visible inconsistencies from the window above.
- We can offer evidence and optional reprocessing of affected requests if you need perfect determinism for auditing/regulatory reasons.

Customer-facing choices (short, actionable):
A) Verify locally (recommended first):
  - Run the attached verification script (see Evidence attachments section) against a representative request or sample response.
  - Check for field presence and token continuity using the CLI snippet below.
B) Request targeted replay (opt-in):
  - If the verification shows inconsistency and you require replay, reply to this message with: tenant-id, time-range (2029-05-12T09:50Z to 2029-05-12T11:10Z), and a preferred replay window.
  - Replays are rate-limited; larger replays may be scheduled. We will attach a replay manifest and integrity signature when complete.
C) No action (recommended for most):
  - If your app tolerated the transient inconsistencies or you already perform downstream reconciliation, no further action is required.

Quick verification checklist for partner engineers (copy/paste friendly):
- 1) Pull logs for tenant-id around 2029-05-12T10:00Z (Log stream: /inference/streaming).
- 2) Run schema validator: rust-cli validate-schema --input response.json --schema streaming-v2.
- 3) Confirm: no missing required fields, token continuity score >= 0.98.

Evidence attachments we will provide after you opt-in or request them explicitly:
- Signed replay-manifest (SHA256) for the time window.
- Sample request/response pairs (anonymized where needed).
- Operator timeline and internal guardrail changes (redacted).

Replay vs Rollback (short guidance):
- Replay: server-side re-execution of your original requests with the current stable runtime to regenerate responses. Preserves original request metadata; recommended when you need corrected outputs but want to retain original timestamps.
- Rollback: re-running an older runtime to reproduce historical behavior. Only offered in exceptional regulatory cases; limited retention and slower.

Operational constraints and expected SLAs for replays:
- Small replays (<10k requests) typically completed within 24 hours.
- Medium replays (10k–1M) scheduled with partner; completion within 3–7 business days depending on queueing and tenant throughput.
- Large replays require a reserved batch window and may incur charges or credits; we will surface options after initial review.

How we validated the fix (summary):
- Continuous batching and token-consistency tests replayed a curated prompt set; all green.
- A/B comparison against a control pool confirmed token-order and structured field stability.
- Canary traffic for 90 minutes post-fix showed error rate parity across regions.

Status updates cadence and next touchpoints:
- Short status update (this note): immediate.
- Operational postmortem (public redacted version) planned for 2029-05-20.
- Partner-specific closure note + replay manifest (if requested) within 48 hours of opt-in.

Contact & escalation path:
- Primary: Maya Thompson (Customer Success) — maya@redwood.ai — Slack: @mthompson (DM or #inc-ops).
- Technical liaison: Diego Alvarez (Eng on-call) — diego@redwood.ai.
- For legal/compliance questions: Priya Nair (Security & Compliance).

Internal notes to self / remaining open items (transparency):
- Confirm log retention windows for affected tenants (action: Evan Brooks).
- Finalize replay signing format and verification CLI (action: Eng-batch).
- Decide on limited SLA credit offering for large customers requesting replays (finance + cs discussion).

Operator checklist (for CS + Eng before external send):
- [ ] Confirm affected tenant list from /inference/alerts export.
- [ ] Run smoke verification per tenant sample.
- [ ] Prepare replay-manifest template and generate initial signatures.
- [ ] Approve partner note language with legal for regulated customers.

Notes about tone and distribution: keep language concise, avoid technical jargon where possible for non-engineering recipients; include CLI/technical snippets in an appendix or as separate attachments.

Appendix (CLI snippets for partner engineers) — include as attachment in customer message:
1) Pull responses: redwood-cli logs fetch --tenant TENANT --from 2029-05-12T09:50Z --to 2029-05-12T11:10Z --path /inference/streaming > responses.ndjson
2) Simple token continuity check (python): python tools/token_continuity_check.py responses.ndjson

Draft message for status page / partner email (short):
Subject: Service incident in eu-west-1 (May 12) — verification & optional replay available
Body: We detected a transient consistency issue affecting a subset of streaming responses on May 12. The issue is resolved and monitoring is back to baseline. If you need us to reprocess requests from the affected window to regenerate corrected responses, please reply with tenant-id and time range. We can also provide signed evidence packages for audit.

-- end of draft --

Revision history:
- 2029-05-12: initial incident note (Maya).
- 2029-05-12 11:30: added rollback vs replay guidance (Diego).
- 2029-06-01: updated SLAs and verification checklist after internal review (Priya).
